description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/cartesian_uniform_1d/rules/weno5_D_inflow_bc (open-boundary WENO5: fifth-order WENO5-Z interior, reduced-order WENO3 one-sided inflow-ghost reconstruction at the left wall, non-reflecting zeroth-order extrapolation at the right wall) driven by problems/advection_1d_inflow_weno5.esm (model AdvectionWENO5Inflow), loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4) -- no per-resolution fixture files. The manufactured steady solution cos(pi x) is SMOOTH and MONOTONE (no interior extrema), so the interior WENO weights stay near-optimal and the recorded L2/Linf errors at t=0.1 are governed by the ONE-SIDED, reduced-order (WENO3, third-order) boundary reconstruction and the prescribed-inflow / extrapolation wall-flux closures, NOT the fifth-order interior. HONEST BOUNDARY-REDUCED ORDER (pinned from the Julia golden, NOT the nominal interior 5): the fifth-order interior sits behind a small O(1)-count set of lower-order boundary cells, so the observed order is well below 5 and rises PRE-ASYMPTOTICALLY as the grid refines and the interior term overtakes the (small-constant) boundary term. The Julia golden gives pairwise orders over N=16->32->64->128 of L2 [2.19, 2.69, 3.66] (median 2.69) and Linf [1.77, 2.09, 3.62] (median 2.09) -- norm-dependent because Linf tracks the single worst (boundary) cell while L2 averages the mostly-fifth-order interior. expected_order 2.4 brackets both norm medians (deviation 0.29 in L2, 0.31 in Linf); order_tolerance is widened to 0.4 (above the 0.2 typical) precisely because this is a mixed-order boundary-reduced scheme whose median-pairwise order is norm-dependent and not yet asymptotic at these resolutions -- it is emphatically NOT a fifth-order claim.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: Same huge nonlinear WENO5-Z reconstruction RHS (stencils/weno5_recon, repeated per face, plus the WENO3 boundary reconstruction) that hangs earthsci-toolkit-rs's diffsol integrator on the periodic WENO5 case (tests/conformance/convergence/advection_1d_periodic_weno5): diffsol has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, so on this large nonlinear RHS it drives dt->0 without terminating instead of erroring. Blocked by structural analogy to the periodic WENO5 sweep (identical reconstruction chain); Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) solve it. Remove once the Rust solver gains a step guard / is verified on this case.
